instructions: Choose the reader’s language, read the relevant workflow and endpoint, then consult its exact OpenAPI contract. Cite the sources you used. These exports do not grant permission to make live business requests.
Preserve the published hosts, methods, paths, authentication, field names, types, required and nullable fields, enums, defaults, limits, and response codes. Translations describe the same API.
schemaScope: This corpus contains guides and operation descriptions. It does not embed every request and response schema. Read the linked OpenAPI contract before generating a request.

Update conversation details including participants, status, and name.

pages.title: Retrieve conversations with flexible filtering options
pages.description:
Retrieve conversations with flexible filtering options.

Can search by external user identifiers (ID, email, phone) or internal participants,
with support for pagination and status filtering.

pages.title: Creates a new conversation with flexible user identification
pages.description:
Create a new conversation with flexible user identification.

External users can be identified by ID, email, or phone.
Internal users are only assigned when explicitly specified; otherwise, conversations are
auto-assigned by round-robin through a team or left open for any available internal user.

When no line is free and the Contacts have a released conversation with exactly the requested participants,
that conversation is recovered and returned instead, keeping its `id` and history. The request's `name` and
`status` are not applied to it.

pages.description: Release a conversation: mark as released, remove external participants, move to RELEASED section.

pages.title: Create a new message
pages.description:
Create a new message within a specified conversation.

For a text message or an uploaded attachment, include all required fields: `conversationId`, `messageBody`, and `enableExternalBroadcast`. Attach uploaded files with their returned identifiers in `mediaIds`; see [Send an attachment](/guides/send-attachments). A successful response returns `messageId`; it does not contain a provider delivery receipt. See [Responses and retries](/guides/responses).

pages.title: Retrieve a contact by an identifier
pages.description:
Get a specific contact by any of its identifiers within the workspace.

`type=ID` returns the same contact as GET /contacts/{contactId}, which is the canonical
URL for a contact and the one to prefer when the id is what you hold.

pages.title: Create presigned uploads for files
pages.description:
Upload an attachment, such as a PDF, image, or document, before creating a message. This operation returns presigned PUT data; the file bytes are uploaded separately. After the upload succeeds, use the returned `mediaId` in the sending operation. Follow [Send an attachment](/guides/send-attachments) for the checksum, upload, and message steps. Generates presigned URLs to upload files (Presigned PUT). Validates extension, contentType, and type-specific limits. Checksum required: send SHA-256 digest in checksumBase64 (Base64). Upload must include header x-amz-checksum-sha256 with the same value. --- To upload your files, you MUST use the returned presigned URL with the HTTP PUT method. Ensure that you upload the file exactly to the URL indicated, without modifications (as required by AWS S3 Presigned URL PUT usage). Refer to the official AWS S3 documentation on Presigned PUT URLs for details: [AWS S3 Presigned PUT Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/PresignedUrlUploadObject.html). Be sure to include all required headers as specified in the response (e.g., 'x-amz-checksum-sha256' with the correct SHA-256 value). If you fail to use the correct HTTP method or headers, AWS will reject the upload request.

pages.title: Retrieve custom attributes by workspaceid
pages.description:
Return the custom attributes for the specified workspace.

By default, only **active** attributes are returned (those without a past `deletedAt`).

**Filters:**
- `category` — Filter by `OPEN` or `CLOSED`. Omit to return all categories.
- `includeArchived` — Set to `true` to include archived attributes
  (those with a past `deletedAt`). Default: `false`.
- `isRequired` — Set to `true` to return only required attributes,
  `false` for optional only. Omit to return all.

pages.title: Get provider channels by workspace id
pages.description:
Get provider channels by workspace identifier.

This response exposes each channel's `provider` and phone-like `identifier`; it does not return a `providerChannelId`. For an Agent's lines, read `agents[].lines[].providerChannelId` from the Agents list. Do not substitute a phone number for a channel ID. See [Concepts and IDs](/guides/identifiers).

pages.title: Get provider channels by workspace id and provider type
pages.description: Get provider channels by workspace identifier and provider type.

pages.title: Initiate a leadscout outbound conversation with a known lead
pages.description:
Start a LeadScout outbound conversation with a known Contact. The Contact must already exist. Bridge resolves a prospecting Agent for an eligible WhatsApp line. The template is referenced by template.id or template.name; the id wins when both are supplied. It must exist and be APPROVED, and any handoffOverride Bridge User must be valid.

An explicit contact.providerChannelId is respected. Without one, automatic selection prefers a free line, then a released recoverable conversation with this Contact, then an occupied active conversation only when forceSend=true. Availability is per Contact on each line, not global line occupancy.

forceSend=true reuses an eligible active conversation; it does not ignore it or create a fresh one. A successful reuse returns alreadyInitiated=true and persists the new template and follow-ups. A recoverable released conversation can be recovered with either value, retains its ID, and returns recovered=true. Blocked and released nonrecoverable conversations are not made usable by this flag. The legacy route can reuse a conversation held by a human or another Agent; unlike Agents outbound, it does not enforce the requested-Agent controller check.

A nonexpired open LeadScout session still blocks a new outbound request with 409 BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0017; inability to finalize an expired session returns 409 BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0018. Other validation still applies. Additional messages are persisted; persistence does not prove delivery or a wait for the lead to reply. A failed request can leave partial work, so do not treat forceSend as idempotency or blindly retry an uncertain result.

See [the complete outbound guide](/guides/agent-outbound) for the false/true matrix, response flags, differences from Agents outbound, errors and handoff.

pages.title: Request a manual handoff of a leadscout conversation to internal users
pages.description:
Request a manual handoff of a LeadScout-controlled conversation to one or more internal users.

The request is acknowledged with `202 Accepted`; assignment is processed asynchronously.
The response echoes the requested assignees and a tracking id for correlation. Internal-user
resolution (by ID or EMAIL) happens downstream and is not reflected in this response.

pages.title: Discover a templates agnostic variable inventory
pages.description:
Return a template's variables — agnostic `key`/`label`/`callerMustSupply`/`isCustom`/`default`.

Never a Meta slot address or index.

`templateId` accepts either the template's `id` or its `name`. Outbound operations accept `template.id` or `template.name`, with a nonblank id taking precedence. Conversation onboarding uses `onboardingTemplates[].templateId`. Use the selector required by the sending operation. See [the template recipe](/guides/send-template).

A variable with `callerMustSupply: true` has no declared source — the caller must include
its `key` in `parameters` when sending, or the send fails with a 422 naming that same `key`.
A variable with `callerMustSupply: false` is either resolved by Bridge on its own (e.g. the
recipient's first name) or already has a value the caller may optionally override.
A variable with `isCustom: true` is a value only the caller knows, with a `default`: send it in
`parameters` to use your own value, or leave it out (or blank) and `default` goes out.

Error codes:
- BRIDGE_CORE_0301: workspace in the path does not match the caller's own workspace (403)
- BRIDGE_TEMPLATE_0001: no PROVIDER_TEMPLATE found for this workspace and identifier — covers
  an unknown id/name, a template that belongs to another workspace, and a template that is
  not a PROVIDER_TEMPLATE, identically (404); this endpoint never confirms the existence of
  a template outside the caller's own workspace

pages.title: Retrieve an internal user by an identifier
pages.description:
Get a specific Bridge User by any of its identifiers within the workspace.

`type=ID` returns the same user as GET /users/{userId}, which is the canonical URL for an

pages.title: Retrieve an internal user by id
pages.description: Get a specific internal user (human agent) by its unique identifier within the workspace.

pages.title: List internal users
pages.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of internal users within the workspace.

Ordered by creation date. The `email` and `status` filters are deprecated and will be removed; to find one internal user by an identifier, use /users/lookup.

pages.title: List the agents of a workspace
pages.description:
List the workspace's Agents with their status, availability and lines.

Every Agent is listed whatever its status; `available` tells whether it can start conversations.
A page can hold fewer than `limit` items; keep paging while `cursor` is not null.

pages.title: Start an outbound conversation with a contact as a given agent
pages.description:
Start an outbound conversation with a known Contact, answered by the given Agent.

Works for LeadScout and Service Agents. The Contact is resolved first, then the Agent, which must exist in
the workspace and be available (see `GET /agents`). The template is referenced by `template.id` or
`template.name` (the id wins when both are sent), must exist and be APPROVED, and a
`handoffOverride` Bridge User must be valid. If `template.media.mediaId` is unknown, the request fails
with 400 `BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0016` only after the conversation was created or recovered, so a retry after
that error may answer differently. Body rules (`consent.status=GRANTED` without `capturedAt`, `template.media`
without exactly one of `mediaId` or `url`) fail with 400 `BRIDGE_CORE_0103`.

The conversation opens on one of the Agent's active WhatsApp lines, controlled by the Agent, with the template
as its first message. A line is picked in this order:
- A free line.
- Otherwise, a line holding a released conversation with this Contact that can be recovered. Recovering
  returns `recovered=true` and replaces the previous outbound context and `agentContext`. This happens even
  with `forceSend=false`.
- Otherwise, when no line is free or recoverable: `forceSend=false` (default) fails with 409
  `BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0008`; `forceSend=true` reuses a line occupied by an active conversation with this
  Contact, preferring one this Agent controls. If the chosen conversation is held by another Agent or a
  Bridge User, the call fails with 409 `BRIDGE_AI_AGENT_OUTBOUND_0006` and nothing is written. Release it
  first, then retry. Lines whose conversation is blocked or was released without recovery are never used, so
  if no line is occupied by an active conversation the call fails with 409 `BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0008` even
  with `forceSend=true`.

`contact.providerChannelId` is a preference: the pinned line is used when it is free or recoverable;
otherwise the same order applies over all the Agent's lines. Among occupied lines, one this Agent controls
comes first; if none does, the pinned line is the one reused (and may fail with 0006).

Reusing a conversation depends on the Agent type:
- LeadScout: if its LeadScout session is still open and not expired, the call fails with 409
  `BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0017` (`extra` carries `conversationId`, `sessionId` and `stage`). If an expired
  session cannot be finalized, it fails with 409 `BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0018`.
- Service Agent: an open, unexpired service session is continued; an expired one is closed as abandoned and a
  new one opens.

See [the complete outbound guide](/guides/agent-outbound) for prerequisites, the forceSend decision table, recovery, partial work and safe retry decisions.

pages.title: List the pipelines of a workspace
pages.description:
List the active pipelines of the workspace, sorted by label.

`isDefault` marks the pipeline `POST /records` uses when no `pipelineId` is sent, and `acceptsApiRecords`
whether a pipeline takes records created through this API.

pages.title: Retrieve a pipeline with its stages and attributes
pages.description:
Get an active pipeline with its current version: stages in order, attributes and active close reasons.

Use it to know which `stageId` and `values` keys `POST /records` accepts.

pages.title: List pipeline records
pages.description:
List records of the workspace, most recently updated first, found in exactly one way.

- `externalId`, with an optional `pipelineId` (the default pipeline otherwise): the one record your system
  created with that id, or none. No cursor follows.
- One of `contactId`, `contactPhone` or `contactEmail`: the records of that contact, optionally narrowed to a
  `pipelineId` and a `stageId`. The narrowing applies to each page read, so a page may hold fewer than
  `limit` records, or none, while a `cursor` still follows it: keep reading until `cursor` is null.
- `pipelineId` alone: the records of that pipeline, optionally narrowed to a `stageId`.

Any other combination fails with 422.

pages.title: Create a pipeline record
pages.description:
Create a record of a contact in a pipeline, such as a sales opportunity.

The contact is given by exactly one of `id`, `phone` or `email` and must exist: it is never created (404
`BRIDGE_EXTERNAL_0001`). `pipelineId` defaults to the workspace's default pipeline and `stageId` to the
pipeline's initial stage. A missing or blank `name` defaults to the contact's full name, then its cellphone,
then its email. Only open stages are accepted, and only `RECORD`-scope attributes of the pipeline's current
version in `values` (a `null`, a blank text or an empty list is left out); every problem found is listed in `extra.errors` of the 422
`BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0311`. When the stage the record starts in requires a complete contact (first name, last name,
cellphone and every required custom attribute of the workspace), an incomplete one fails with 422
`BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0305`, whose `extra.missing` names what it lacks. A second record with the same `externalId`
in the pipeline fails with 409 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0003`, whose `extra.recordId` is the existing record.

`Idempotency-Key` is required. Retrying with the same key and body answers 201 with the first record and
`Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The same key with a different body fails with 422 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0402`, and
while the first request is still running with 409 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0401`. When the request fails, the key is
freed and can be retried. If the first request was cut off before it finished, its key keeps answering 409
`BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0401` for up to 24 hours: retry with a new key, and send `externalId` so that a retry never
creates a second record.

pages.title: Retrieve a pipeline record
pages.description: Get a record of the workspace by its id.

pages.title: Update a pipeline record
pages.description:
Change the name or some values of a record, open or closed.

Only the fields sent change: a missing `name` keeps the name, and the attributes left out of `values` keep their
value; a `null`, a blank text or an empty list removes a value. A record always has a name, so a `null` or blank
`name` fails like any other invalid field. Every problem found is listed in `extra.errors` of the 422
`BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0311`, which is also the answer to a body that changes nothing. A change that leaves the record
as it is writes nothing and answers the record. With `expectedRevision`, a record changed since you read it fails
with 409 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0101`, whose `extra.currentRecord` is the record as it is now.

pages.title: Move a pipeline record to another stage
pages.description:
Move an open record to another stage of the pipeline version it follows; a final stage closes it.

A stage that is not in that version, such as one of another pipeline, fails with 422 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0311`
(`errRecordStage`), and the stage the record is already in with 409 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0004`. A closed record
fails with 409 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0306`: reopen it first. When the stage requires a complete contact, an
incomplete one fails with 422 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0305`. A move to a final stage may carry an active `reasonId`
of the pipeline (422 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0315` when it does not exist, `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0314` when it is retired)
and a `reasonNote`; without one the record closes with no reason. A reason or a note on a move to an open
stage fails with 422 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0311`. With `expectedRevision`, a record changed since you read it fails
with 409 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0101`, whose `extra.currentRecord` is the record as it is now.

`Idempotency-Key` is required and works like on `POST /records`: a retry with the same key and body answers the
record with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, as it is now. The same key on another record or operation fails with
422 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0402`.

pages.title: Reopen a closed pipeline record
pages.description:
Take a closed record back to the open stage it was in before it was closed, and clear its close reason.

When its history names no open stage of its version, the record goes to the pipeline's initial stage. An open
record fails with 409 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0307`. When that stage requires a complete contact, an incomplete one
fails with 422 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0305`. The body is optional; with `expectedRevision`, a record changed since you
read it fails with 409 `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0101`, whose `extra.currentRecord` is the record as it is now.

`Idempotency-Key` is required and works like on `POST /records/{recordId}/move`.

pages.title: Register a campaign lead
pages.description: Registers a lead captured by a tenant's landing page and queues the first outbound WhatsApp message. A 202 means the lead was accepted, not that a message was sent.
